summary: Provides a thesaurus mapping MPLS-TP terminology into the context of ITU-T transport network recommendations, noting MPLS-TP applies in wider contexts than transport networks. It is informational and is meant to reduce confusion between two communities.

eli5.summary: A dictionary between two groups who use different words for the same things.

subtitle: Bridging terminology between MPLS-TP and ITU-T transport networks

tldr.problem: The IETF MPLS-TP specification and ITU-T Transport Network recommendations use different terminology for similar concepts due to their different historical backgrounds.
tldr.mechanism: This thesaurus maps MPLS-TP terms to their equivalents in ITU-T transport network context, helping both communities understand each other's specifications.
tldr.outcome: Engineers from the IETF and ITU-T communities can collaborate more effectively on transport network deployments using MPLS-TP.

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: Help both communities understand each other

today: RFC 7087 is an informational reference that remains relevant for anyone working on transport networks that use MPLS-TP specifications. It serves as a bridge between IETF and ITU-T protocol communities.

sections.title: Why Two Communities Need a Dictionary
sections.content:
The MPLS Transport Profile (MPLS-TP) is a set of MPLS and Pseudowire functions designed for Transport Network environments. It was developed by the IETF drawing on Internet protocols. The ITU-T (the United Nations telecom standardization body) has defined its own Transport Network architecture based on decades of telephone-industry standards.

Because of this different heritage, the two communities use different terminology even when describing identical concepts. For example, what MPLS calls a Label Switched Path relates to what ITU-T calls a Transport Path.

This RFC provides a thesaurus (compared in IETF circles to the Rosetta Stone) to help readers translate between the two terminologies. The definitions do not claim to be exclusive or complete, but rather show how MPLS-TP concepts fit within ITU-T's framework.
sections.eli5: The Internet engineers and the telephone engineers built networks differently and use different vocabulary. This book explains how their terms connect.

sections.title: The Thesaurus Contents
sections.content:
The document defines about 48 key terms in MPLS-TP and their ITU-T equivalents. Key concepts include:

Path concepts: A transport path (MPLS: LSP or PW) carries traffic in one or both directions. An associated bidirectional path uses two separate unidirectional paths (one per direction) that may take different routes. A co-routed bidirectional path uses the same route for both directions (typical in transport networks).

Management concepts: Maintenance entities (ME) are the target of monitoring and management. A maintenance entity group (MEG) contains one or more MEs. Maintenance entity group end points (MEPs) are the boundaries of MEs; intermediate points (MIPs) are between them.

Layer concepts: A layer network is a logical construction in which a higher client layer uses services from a lower server layer. Transmission media layers consist of section and physical layers. Sublayers are internal to a layer and not directly accessible to clients.

Recovery concepts: End-to-end recovery restores entire paths; link recovery restores individual hops; segment recovery restores portions of paths.
sections.eli5: The thesaurus covers paths (how traffic flows), management (how to monitor), layers (how services stack), and recovery (how to fix failures).

sections.title: Architecture Building Blocks
sections.content:
The RFC organizes MPLS-TP concepts into logical categories. Segments and concatenated segments are portions of paths. Bidirectional paths can be associated (separate unidirectional paths) or co-routed (same path both ways). Domains group network entities for administrative or managerial purposes, similar to IGP areas or Autonomous Systems.

Ring topologies can be physical (using physical links) or logical (using MPLS-TP tunnels or pseudowires as data links). Communication channels (DCN, ECC, SCC, MCC) carry management, signaling, and operations traffic separately from the main data path.
sections.eli5: MPLS-TP organizes networks into pieces (segments), paths (bidirectional), and groups (domains and rings), with separate channels for management.

sections.title: Operations and Monitoring
sections.content:
The thesaurus defines operations terms critical for running MPLS-TP networks. Faults, defects, and failures have precise meanings: a fault is the inability to perform a function, a defect is a high density of anomalies, and a failure is a detected fault.

Operations Support Systems (OSS) perform OAM&P functions including surveillance and testing. Monitoring verifies path performance through OAM flows, path segment tunnels, or tandem connection monitoring. Protection entities and working entities support recovery: protection entities are pre-allocated, while recovery entities are used after a failure.
sections.eli5: When monitoring networks, engineers track faults (broken things), defects (many small problems), and organize recovery using pre-planned protection paths.
